title: Second conditional
note: Unreal or unlikely present: If I had more time, I would learn Italian. Czech kdybych + conditional produces *If I would have more time word for word - that is the whole target error. a2_first_conditional is the real-possibility one; third and mixed stay B2. If I were you is taught as a fixed phrase for advice. Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): 15 new, both clause orders, negatives in each half (would not say / did not have to), two more If I were you advice items, and questions. Rules applied this pass: A8 the would twin ('d) is now in accepts on every result half; A4 all four cleared (a million, more money, go out more often, and the Czech demonstrative on `tu odpoved`); F3 earlier / jobs swapped for at six / her job. KNOWN LINT FALSE POSITIVE: the seven remaining A8 flags all want *If I'd more time* / *If I'd a car* as the twin of `if I had ...`. Lexical had does not contract in modern English, so those accepts do not exist and must not be added - same lint gap as had-to on b1_past_modals and the negative tags on b1_question_tags. Queued in DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Second conditional
points: The past form does not mean the past. It means: this is not true now.

examples.en: **If** I had time, I **would** learn Italian.
examples.cz: Kdybych měl čas, učil bych se italsky.

examples.en: What **would** you do if you won?

cards.title: would never goes in the if half
cards.title_cz: would nikdy nepatří do části s if
points: Czech puts the conditional in both parts. English puts it in one.

cards.title: first or second?
points: Real chance → the first kind. Imaginary → this one.

rows: it is not going to, but imagine

cards.title: If I were you
points: **were** is used for every person in this phrase.
~~If I was you~~ is not the set form.

rows: **If I** were you, I'd take the job.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: One half gets **would**. The **if** half gets the past form.

rows: ~~If I would have more time, I would learn Italian.~~
**If** I **had** more time, I would learn Italian.
~~If I will win, I would buy a house.~~
~~If I was you, I'd take the job.~~
**If I** were you, I'd take the job.
~~I would to go if I had time.~~
I **would** go if I had time.

items.en: If I had more time, I would learn Italian.
items.cz: Kdybych měl víc času, učil bych se italsky.
items.gap: If I ____ more time, I would learn Italian. (have)
accepts: If I had more time, I would learn Italian.
If I had more time, I'd learn Italian.
items.wrong: If I would have more time, I would learn Italian.
items.explanation: The **if** half takes the past form **had**. would belongs in the other half.
items.explanation_cz: Část s **if** má minulý tvar **had**. would patří do druhé části.

items.en: What would you do if you won a million?
items.cz: Co bys dělal, kdybys vyhrál milion?
items.gap: What ____ you do if you won a million? (will / would)
accepts: What would you do if you won a million?
items.explanation: The result half takes **would** + the plain verb do.
items.explanation_cz: Výsledková část má **would** + základní tvar do.
items.wrong: What will you do if you won a million?

items.en: If I were you, I'd take the job.
items.cz: Být tebou, vzal bych tu práci.
items.gap: If I ____ you, I'd take the job. (be)
accepts: If I were you, I'd take the job.
If I were you, I would take the job.
items.wrong: If I was you, I'd take the job.
items.explanation: **If I were you** is the fixed phrase for advice.
items.explanation_cz: **If I were you** je ustálená fráze pro radu.

items.en: If he came at six, we would have more time.
items.cz: Kdyby přišel v šest, měli bychom víc času.
items.gap: If he ____ at six, we would have more time. (come)
accepts: If he came at six, we would have more time.
If he came at six, we'd have more time.
items.wrong: If he would come at six, we would have more time.
items.explanation: Past form **came** in the if half, not would come.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý tvar **came** v části s if, ne would come.

items.en: I would buy a bigger flat if I had more money.
items.cz: Koupil bych si větší byt, kdybych měl víc peněz.
items.gap: I ____ a bigger flat if I had more money. (buy)
accepts: I would buy a bigger flat if I had more money.
I'd buy a bigger flat if I had more money.
items.explanation: **would** + the plain verb **buy**, with no to.
items.explanation_cz: **would** + základní tvar **buy**, bez to.
items.wrong: I would to buy a bigger flat if I had more money.

items.en: If I lived in London, I would go out more often.
items.cz: Kdybych bydlel v Londýně, chodil bych častěji ven.
items.gap: If I ____ in London, I would go out more often. (live)
accepts: If I lived in London, I would go out more often.
If I lived in London, I'd go out more often.
items.explanation: **lived** — the past form marks it as not true now.
items.explanation_cz: **lived** — minulý tvar značí, že to teď neplatí.
items.wrong: If I would live in London, I would go out more often.

items.en: She would be happier if she changed her job.
items.cz: Byla by šťastnější, kdyby změnila práci.
items.gap: She ____ happier if she changed her job. (be)
accepts: She would be happier if she changed her job.
She'd be happier if she changed her job.
items.explanation: **would be** in the result half.
items.explanation_cz: **would be** ve výsledkové části.
items.wrong: She will be happier if she changed her job.

items.en: If it rained, we would stay at home.
items.cz: Kdyby pršelo, zůstali bychom doma.
items.gap: If it ____, we would stay at home. (rain)
accepts: If it rained, we would stay at home.
If it rained, we'd stay at home.
items.wrong: If it will rain, we would stay at home.
items.explanation: Imagining, not predicting, so **rained** and would stay.
items.explanation_cz: Představa, ne předpověď, takže **rained** a would stay.

items.en: What would you say if she asked you?
items.cz: Co bys řekl, kdyby se tě zeptala?
items.gap: What would you say if she ____ you? (ask)
accepts: What would you say if she asked you?
items.explanation: The **if** half stays in the past form: asked.
items.explanation_cz: Část s **if** zůstává v minulém tvaru: asked.

items.en: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
items.cz: Kdybych znal tu odpověď, řekl bych ti.
items.gap: If I ____ the answer, I would tell you. (know)
accepts: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
If I knew the answer, I'd tell you.
items.wrong: If I would know the answer, I would tell you.
items.explanation: **knew** in the if half. The point is that I do not know it.
items.explanation_cz: **knew** v části s if. Jde o to, že ji neznám.

items.en: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
items.cz: Kdybych měl auto, jezdil bych do práce autem.
items.gap: If I ____ a car, I would drive to work. (have)
accepts: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
If I had a car, I'd drive to work.
items.wrong: If I would have a car, I would drive to work.
items.explanation: The **if** half takes the past form **had**. Only the other half gets would.
items.explanation_cz: Část s **if** má minulý tvar **had**. Would patří jen do té druhé.

items.en: If she spoke better English, she would get the job.
items.cz: Kdyby uměla líp anglicky, tu práci by dostala.
items.gap: If she ____ better English, she would get the job. (speak)
accepts: If she spoke better English, she would get the job.
If she spoke better English, she'd get the job.
items.wrong: If she would speak better English, she would get the job.
items.explanation: **spoke** is the past form doing unreal work: she does not speak better English.
items.explanation_cz: **spoke** je minulý tvar v nereálné roli: líp anglicky neumí.

items.en: I would help you if I had time.
items.cz: Pomohl bych ti, kdybych měl čas.
items.gap: I ____ you if I had time. (help)
accepts: I would help you if I had time.
I'd help you if I had time.
items.wrong: I would to help you if I had time.
items.explanation: **would** + the plain verb **help** — no *to* after would.
items.explanation_cz: **would** + základní tvar **help** — po would není žádné *to*.

items.en: If I were you, I would talk to your boss.
items.cz: Být tebou, promluvil bych si se šéfem.
items.gap: If I ____ you, I would talk to your boss. (be)
accepts: If I were you, I would talk to your boss.
If I were you, I'd talk to your boss.
items.wrong: If I was you, I would talk to your boss.
items.explanation: In this advice phrase the form is **were** for every person, including I.
items.explanation_cz: V téhle radě je tvar **were** pro každou osobu, i pro I.

items.en: If I were you, I would not wait.
items.cz: Být tebou, nečekal bych.
items.gap: If I ____ you, I would not wait. (be)
accepts: If I were you, I would not wait.
If I were you, I wouldn't wait.
items.wrong: If I was you, I would not wait.
items.explanation: **If I were you** is fixed. The advice half can be negative: **would not** wait.
items.explanation_cz: **If I were you** je ustálené. Rada může být záporná: **would not** wait.

items.en: He would not say that if he knew you.
items.cz: Neřekl by to, kdyby tě znal.
items.gap: He ____ that if he knew you. (not / say)
accepts: He would not say that if he knew you.
He wouldn't say that if he knew you.
items.wrong: He would not said that if he knew you.
items.explanation: Negative result half: **would not** + the plain verb **say**.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná druhá část: **would not** + základní tvar **say**.

items.en: We would not go if it snowed.
items.cz: Nejeli bychom, kdyby sněžilo.
items.gap: We would not go if it ____. (snow)
accepts: We would not go if it snowed.
We wouldn't go if it snowed.
items.wrong: We would not go if it would snow.
items.explanation: Even after a negative result, the **if** half keeps the past form: **snowed**.
items.explanation_cz: I po záporné druhé části má část s **if** minulý tvar: **snowed**.

items.en: If they invited me, I would go.
items.cz: Kdyby mě pozvali, šel bych.
items.gap: If they ____ me, I would go. (invite)
accepts: If they invited me, I would go.
If they invited me, I'd go.
items.wrong: If they would invite me, I would go.
items.explanation: **invited** in the if half, **would go** in the other. One conditional, not two.
items.explanation_cz: **invited** v části s if, **would go** v druhé. Jeden kondicionál, ne dva.

items.en: What would you do if you lost your job?
items.cz: Co bys dělal, kdybys přišel o práci?
items.gap: What ____ you do if you lost your job? (will / would)
accepts: What would you do if you lost your job?
items.wrong: What will you do if you lost your job?
items.explanation: The question half takes **would**; the **if** half stays past: *lost*.
items.explanation_cz: Tázací část má **would**; část s **if** zůstává v minulém tvaru: *lost*.

items.en: If my brother had a bigger flat, we would stay with him.
items.cz: Kdyby měl brácha větší byt, bydleli bychom u něj.
items.gap: If my brother ____ a bigger flat, we would stay with him. (have)
accepts: If my brother had a bigger flat, we would stay with him.
If my brother had a bigger flat, we'd stay with him.
items.wrong: If my brother would have a bigger flat, we would stay with him.
items.explanation: **had** even in the third person: the if half never takes would.
items.explanation_cz: **had** i ve třetí osobě: část s if nikdy nemá would.

items.en: If you asked her, she would tell you.
items.cz: Kdyby ses jí zeptal, řekla by ti to.
items.gap: If you ____ her, she would tell you. (ask)
accepts: If you asked her, she would tell you.
If you asked her, she'd tell you.
items.wrong: If you would ask her, she would tell you.
items.explanation: **asked** is the unreal past: you are not going to ask.
items.explanation_cz: **asked** je nereálný minulý tvar: ty se nezeptáš.

items.en: If I did not have to work, I would sleep all morning.
items.cz: Kdybych nemusel do práce, spal bych celé dopoledne.
items.gap: If I ____ have to work, I would sleep all morning. (not / do)
accepts: If I did not have to work, I would sleep all morning.
If I did not have to work, I'd sleep all morning.
If I didn't have to work, I would sleep all morning.
If I didn't have to work, I'd sleep all morning.
items.wrong: If I would not have to work, I would sleep all morning.
items.explanation: The negative **if** half is **did not** + plain verb — still the past form, still no would.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná část s **if** je **did not** + základní tvar — pořád minulý tvar, pořád bez would.

items.en: If she had more money, she would buy a house.
items.cz: Kdyby měla víc peněz, koupila by si dům.
items.gap: If she had more money, she ____ a house. (buy)
accepts: If she had more money, she would buy a house.
If she had more money, she'd buy a house.
items.wrong: If she had more money, she would bought a house.
items.explanation: **would** + the plain verb **buy**, never a past form after would.
items.explanation_cz: **would** + základní tvar **buy**, po would nikdy minulý tvar.

items.en: If I had a dog, I would walk every morning.
items.cz: Kdybych měl psa, chodil bych každé ráno na procházku.
items.gap: If I had a dog, I ____ every morning. (walk)
accepts: If I had a dog, I would walk every morning.
If I had a dog, I'd walk every morning.
items.wrong: If I had a dog, I will walk every morning.
items.explanation: The situation is imaginary, so the result is **would walk**, not will walk.
items.explanation_cz: Situace je smyšlená, takže výsledek je **would walk**, ne will walk.

items.en: If we had a bigger table, we would invite everybody.
items.cz: Kdybychom měli větší stůl, pozvali bychom všechny.
items.gap: If we ____ a bigger table, we would invite everybody. (have)
accepts: If we had a bigger table, we would invite everybody.
If we had a bigger table, we'd invite everybody.
items.wrong: If we would have a bigger table, we would invite everybody.
items.explanation: **had** in the if half. Czech puts the conditional in both halves; English puts it in one.
items.explanation_cz: **had** v části s if. Čeština dává kondicionál do obou částí, angličtina jen do jedné.
